name: Abshir-Ata Waterfall
dist: Nookat District, Osh Region, Kulatov rural municipality (aiyl okmotu)
near: Villages of the Kulatov aiyl okmotu in the Abshir-Say gorge (24.kg); per OSM the nearest pin is Kanaka (~0.5 km). It is 10 km to the main road and 70 km to Osh (24.kg); Nookat is ~40 km to the northeast (Nomad's Land).
elev: About 1800 m (Nomad's Land); the valley as a whole is 1500–2500 m (too.kg, Trip to Kyrgyzstan). The cascades are ~15 and ~12 m (I Love KG).
short: Abshir-Ata is a sacred karst waterfall in the Abshir-Say gorge: the stream bursts out of an opening in a sheer limestone wall, ~70 km from Osh.
desc: Abshir-Ata is a waterfall in the valley of the Abshir-Say river on the northern spurs of the Kichi-Alay Range (Trip to Kyrgyzstan). The water emerges from a small karst cave — a dark opening 1.5–2 m in diameter at a height of 12–15 m — and falls down a sheer rock in two cascades of about 15 and 12 m (Trip to Kyrgyzstan, I Love KG). The water is considered mineral and holy; according to legend, a wanderer struck the rock with his staff and milk flowed from it (Trip to Kyrgyzstan). The place is revered, and pilgrims come here. A good dirt road has been laid in the gorge up to the waterfall, there are guesthouses and cafes nearby, and souvenirs are sold (too.kg). In the area are the Khurkhyz and Chillyakana caves, the sacred spring Kotur-Bulak, a landslide-dammed lake (~10 km) and rock drawings (too.kg).
guide: Abshir-Ata is that rare waterfall that gushes straight out of the rock: the stream bursts from a dark opening at a height of 12–15 m. For locals it is a holy place — according to legend a wanderer struck a stone with his staff and milk flowed out of it — so behave as you would in a mosque: quietly and respectfully. In spring and early summer the flow is strongest; in summer the road is easier but there are more people (I Love KG). Do not stand under the wet overhanging walls — rockfalls happen. If you have time, drop by the sacred spring Kotur-Bulak and the Khurkhyz and Chillyakana caves (too.kg).
see: The stream from an opening in the rock (two cascades of ~15 and ~12 m); the revered holy spring; the Khurkhyz and Chillyakana caves; the Kotur-Bulak spring; the landslide-dammed lake ~10 km away; rock drawings at 5 and 20 km; old mine adits (too.kg, I Love KG).
skip: You have only one day in Osh — the road takes at least 2 h each way (I Love KG). You expect a big “wild” waterfall — this is a pilgrimage site with cafes and souvenirs (too.kg). You are going after heavy rain — the road and wet ledges are dangerous.
diff: Easy–moderate: access by dirt road, a short approach (~3 km up the gorge from the river mouth — Trip to Kyrgyzstan); the last sections are narrow and wet, and non-slip footwear is needed (I Love KG).
when: Late spring — early summer: the stream is most impressive, but the water is higher; dry summer — the road is easier, hotter and more crowded (I Love KG). A winter visit is not described.
hours: A natural/holy site with no opening hours; the cafes and guesthouses operate in season (too.kg); come back in daylight (I Love KG).
daytime: Morning — fewer pilgrims, less heat, light on the rock; plan your return before dark (I Love KG).
how: From Osh west to Nookat and then along local roads into the Abshir-Say gorge — about 70 km, at least 2 h each way (I Love KG). In the gorge there is a good dirt road all the way to the waterfall (too.kg); per Trip to Kyrgyzstan — about 3 km up the gorge from the river mouth. The direction “70 km east of Osh” (too.kg) is wrong: the valley and waterfall lie west–southwest of Osh (longitude ~72.36° versus ~72.80° for Osh); the road goes west through Nookat (I Love KG).
needcar: Yes: a car with a driver who waits, or your own car; there is no direct tourist transport (I Love KG).
self: Yes, in your own/rented car or with a driver: the road to the waterfall is dirt but good (too.kg); on site there are cafes and guesthouses.
roadtype: Paved Osh — Nookat, then local roads; in the gorge a good dirt road to the waterfall (too.kg); mud is possible after rain (I Love KG).
traveltime: Osh → waterfall: ~70 km, at least 2 h each way (I Love KG); on foot ~3 km along the gorge from the mouth (Trip to Kyrgyzstan). The last 10 km are from the main road to the waterfall (24.kg).
stay: Guesthouses and cafes near the waterfall, camping spots (too.kg; Trip to Kyrgyzstan — Guest Houses); names and 2025–2026 prices not found. The main choice of accommodation is in Osh. Per 24.kg (05.2025): the gorge receives “more than 200 thousand” visitors per season, small recreation areas (tapchans, cafes) operate, but there are no proper toilets or hotels.
net: There is no mobile signal in the gorge (too.kg). The operator is not specified.
entry: As of 2025 — free/there was no official fee: 24.kg (21.05.2025) writes that paid entry, parking and toilets are planned to be organized by 2026 under a World Bank project ($500 thousand). Whether a fee was introduced in 2026 and how much is not confirmed; have cash.
transfer: Not confirmed: 2025–2026 prices for a car with a driver Osh — Abshir-Ata were not found (there are no tours from Osh on Sputnik8/CBT). A guide: marshrutka Osh — Uzgen 70–100 som for ~55 km (eurasia.travel forum, 01.2025) — the fare to Nookat is comparable, then a taxi by arrangement.
bring: Water and food, non-slip shoes, a light rain jacket (spray), cash (I Love KG); for a pilgrimage site — covered clothing (editorial). Drink water from the river/lake only after boiling or filtering (too.kg, I Love KG).
warn: Do not stand under overhanging wet walls — rockfall; wet ledges are slippery; high water in spring (I Love KG). There is no signal (too.kg). Claims about the healing effect of the water are not confirmed by medical sources. The Google pin “Apshyr-Ata” ~75 km away is a different place; do not use it for navigation. The direction “70 km east of Osh” (too.kg) is wrong: the valley and waterfall lie west–southwest of Osh (longitude ~72.36° versus ~72.80° for Osh); the road goes west through Nookat (I Love KG). Mudflows on 28.06, 14.07 and 18.07.2024: 5 km of road and 4 of 5 bridges destroyed, 125 houses flooded; on 29.06.2024 more than 1,300 people were evacuated from the recreation area, and 6 people died in the district (Kaktus, 24.kg). As of May 2025 the old bridges were declared unsafe, and restoration was slow (24.kg 21.05.2025) — after downpours and in June–July do not enter the gorge, and watch for Emergencies Ministry warnings.
food: Cafes near the waterfall (too.kg) — national dishes (menu not confirmed); mineral water from springs (too.kg); in Osh and Nookat — Osh plov (editorial).
reviews: No cards with ratings were found on Google/2GIS/TripAdvisor (Google matched a different “Apshyr-Ata”; 07.10.2026). Per 24.kg (05.2025) — more than 200 thousand visitors per season; complaints about the lack of toilets and hotels, unsafe bridges. From videos/blogs: pluses — a unique “waterfall from a rock”, a holy place; minuses — summer crowds, the road.
p.sum: The waterfall is 70 km southwest of Osh (via Nookat, ≥2 h) — do it as a day trip by car with a driver from Osh or in your own car: the last ~10 km are a narrow dirt road (2 km of remaining asphalt + 8 km of single-lane dirt) after the 2024 mudflows. There is no public transport to the waterfall; on site there are seasonal tapchan cafes (raised platforms) and ~24 souvenir stalls, but no proper toilets, hotels or signal. Do not go after downpours and at the peak of floods (June–July).

p.season: April–May — the most powerful stream, high water; June–July — peak of visitors and mudflow risk (the 2024 disasters — 28.06, 14.07, 18.07); August–September — dry, an easier road; winter — a visit is not described.
p.budget.economy: Marshrutka Osh — Nookat + taxi to the waterfall (prices not found); food on a tapchan ~400–600 som
p.budget.comfort: A car with a driver for the day from Osh — price on request
p.permits: Not needed. There was no entrance fee in 2025; paid entry/parking was planned by 2026 under a World Bank project — as of 04.2026 the infrastructure has not been created (time.kg), the introduction of a fee is not confirmed — have cash. Deputies call the area the “Abshyr-Ata national park”.
p.access: With children — yes (a short approach from the recreation area), but slippery rocks; for older people — the recreation area is accessible, the road is bumpy; with a wheelchair — no; with a dog — yes, but there are many people in season.
